title: A Cover for the Asset
premise: Rafael Coldharbour, a deniable analyst discarded by three intelligence agencies, lives off-grid in Lisbon until a burner phone rings with the voice of Mara Voss—the handler who trained them and who officially died two years ago. Mara claims the network that made them both, called the Loom, is preparing to sell its entire asset roster at a black-market summit in Trieste, including Rafael's real identity. Hunted by Loom cleaners and distrusted by the one agency that might help, Rafael must decide whether love for the woman who weaponized them is worth burning every bridge they have left. In the end, Rafael destroys the Loom's ledger at the summit itself, exposes Mara as the summit's architect who used Rafael as her unwitting key, and walks away alive but finally, deliberately visible—choosing belonging over survival.
about_author: Oscar Nakamura is a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade reconstructing other people's lies before turning to fiction. He writes from a rented flat above a shuttered casino, where he insists the best tradecraft stories begin.

chapters.title: The Phone That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Living under a false name in Lisbon, Rafael finds a burner phone in their own mailbox—impossible, since no one knows this address. When it rings, the voice is Mara Voss, dead two years. The beat: dread wrapped in longing; invisibility was always an illusion.

chapters.title: Dead Handlers Tell No Tales
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael verifies Mara's voice against old training tapes and confirms she died in a Prague safehouse fire—or so three agencies' records agree. Flashbacks reveal how deeply she shaped them. Beat: grief resurfacing, suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: Cleaners at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Two Loom cleaners hit Rafael's flat within hours of the call, proving someone tracked the phone to them. Rafael escapes through the tram tunnels with a go-bag built for a life they swore was over. Beat: hunted again, adrenaline masking terror.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Mara (interleaved). In Trieste, Mara reviews the Loom's asset ledger—names, biometrics, prices—for an upcoming private summit of buyers. She flags Rafael's file with a red mark only she understands. Beat: cold calculation hiding a private agenda.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Friends
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael approaches a former contact at the Service, offering information on the Loom in exchange for protection. The contact agrees—then Rafael realizes they've been handed a tracking beacon, not an ally. Beat: bitter confirmation that institutions never loved them back.

chapters.title: What Mara Made
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, heavy flashback. Training years: Mara teaching Rafael to lie, to vanish, to survive interrogation—and one night in Vienna when the professional line blurred into something neither named. Beat: tenderness entangled with manipulation, love as a tradecraft tool.

chapters.title: The Red Mark
chapters.summary: POV Mara. A rival within the Loom, Director Hale, questions why Mara keeps pulling Rafael's file. Mara deflects, but Hale assigns surveillance. We learn Mara engineered the burner call herself. Beat: Mara's control beginning to crack under scrutiny.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Personal Edition
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Using skills Mara taught, Rafael turns the tables on their Service tail and extracts the beacon's destination: a coordination cell feeding the Trieste summit. Beat: grim competence returning; the student outgrowing the lesson.

chapters.title: Second Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The burner rings again. Mara admits she's alive, admits the call was hers, and asks for help destroying the ledger before it sells—including Rafael's file. Rafael refuses and hangs up. Beat: fury and yearning colliding; duty says walk away.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Hale confronts Mara with evidence of her contact with Rafael and offers a deal: deliver Rafael to the summit as a live demonstration asset, or be sold alongside them. Beat: Mara cornered, forced to choose between the network and the person she trained.

chapters.title: The Vienna Precedent
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Digging into the Prague fire, Rafael finds evidence Mara burned her own death—and that Hale ordered a prior asset's assassination using Rafael's signature. Someone has been framing them for years. Beat: righteous anger; the past was never buried.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael tracks down Sefa, a retired Loom courier living openly in Porto, who confirms the summit's date, buyer list, and that Hale plans to purge every asset after the sale. Beat: fragile trust between survivors; belonging found in the discarded.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara leaks Rafael's location to Hale while secretly arranging their extraction route—a double game that requires Rafael to believe she betrayed them. Beat: self-sacrifice disguised as treachery; loneliness as armor.

chapters.title: Captured
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Cleaners take Rafael in Marseille. Interrogated by Hale personally, Rafael learns Mara requested their capture—and feels the last thread of trust snap. Beat: betrayal confirmed, heartbreak weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The Demonstration
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At a pre-summit showcase, Hale presents captured assets to buyers. Mara watches Rafael displayed like inventory and realizes Hale intends to sell Rafael first and burn the rest. Beat: horror crystallizing into commitment; love choosing its side.

chapters.title: The Keyhole
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. In holding, Rafael discovers the ledger vault opens only to a biometric signature from a founding-era asset—Mara's, or the one she cloned from Rafael during training. They are the key. Beat: revelation reframing everything; they were never incidental.

chapters.title: Two Liars, One Plan
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Mara engineers a blackout window; Rafael picks their restraints and reaches the pre-arranged extraction point. Face to face for the first time in years, they trade accusations, then truths, then a plan. Beat: reconciliation without absolution; partnership rebuilt on honesty about damage.

chapters.title: Summit Eve
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Infiltrating the Trieste palazzo via Sefa's courier routes, they map the vault, the buyers, and Hale's kill team. Mara confesses the red mark meant 'protect at all costs.' Beat: quiet before catastrophe; intimacy sharpened by mortality.

chapters.title: The Sale
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The summit convenes. Hale begins auctioning files live. Mara stalls the bidding from inside while Rafael breaches the vault corridor—but Hale springs the trap he'd always planned for her. Beat: peak tension; the con inside the con exposed.

chapters.title: Burn the Loom
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Climax. Rafael fights through Hale's team, forces the vault with their cloned signature, and initiates the ledger's destruction as buyers scatter. Mara takes a bullet meant for Rafael; together they trigger the fire suppression protocol that wipes the archive. Beat: cathartic violence in service of erasure.

chapters.title: Ash and Accountability
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Hale, exposed to his own buyers as the man who sold them compromised goods, is abandoned by everyone. Mara survives, wounded. Rafael hands the surviving fragments—not identities, just proof—to a journalist, ending the Loom's myth of permanence. Beat: justice without triumph; the price tallied honestly.

chapters.title: A Name, Spoken Aloud
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Weeks later, Rafael uses their real name for the first time in a decade—over coffee with Mara, who is learning to exist without a network too. No agencies, no covers, no orders. Beat: resolution; belonging chosen freely, love tested and kept, survival finally worth its cost.
